rv.q: Inspired by the life and music of Gloria and Emilio Estefan, it literally gets the audience off its seats and into a conga line.
Yes, I know, it's just a jukebox musical, but I liked 'On Your Feet!' In fact, I liked it a lot—and I think you might, too.
Newcomer Ana Villafane (who originated the role in the show’s Chicago premiere) is a knockout in the leading role, the dazzling centerpiece of this flashy, splashy spectacle helmed by Jerry Mitchell.
If the Estefans’ musical remains pretty much by-the-numbers, at least those numbers really rock.
This biographical musical is an infectious account of the lives and careers of the Latin music crossover sensation and her producer-musician husband Emilio Estefan.
As story-telling, On Your Feet! can be as clunkily generic as the title.
"On Your Feet!" ultimately falls somewhere in the middle of the hefty pack of jukebox musicals that have plugged in to Broadway's power strip.

"On Your Feet!" feels especially well-timed and unusual, in that it's a show that both sides of that debate can appreciate — as they can the genuinely remarkable couple whose collective career is celebrated.
The problem, which may not be a problem for many who have already pushed the advance sales into big numbers, is the by-the-numbers story.
To say that On Your Feet! is better than most of its ilk is therefore faint praise; it means you might have almost as good a time as you would if it were merely a concert.
But there are few other enticements in On Your Feet!
Neither Estefan nor her life nor her music are especially dramatically interesting.
The result is a perfect 10. Fun, tears, greats songs and dancing.
This exuberant and shrewdly conceived formulaic jukebox musical about the lives of Gloria and Emilio Estefan contains all of their hits with Miami Sound Machine.
Well, they conquered the music charts, and now they're extending that success to the Broadway stage.
Thank Ana Villafane, whose charisma and energy on stage, coupled with a powerful voice, knocks the role of Gloria Estefan out of the park.
As long promised, the rhythm does indeed get you.
"While the dramatic merits and execution of the performance as a whole fall short, there's no denying 'On Your Feet' is a fun, engaging spectacle.
Villafañe and the Emilio of Josh Segarra, who has that untranslatable appeal that Cubans call sabor, are so winning that you find yourself forgiving the lapses.

In the genre of so-called jukebox musicals based on singers and/or popular songs (Beautiful, Jersey Boys, Mamma Mia), On Your Feet fares well as a cohesive blend of story-telling via this singer’s pantheon of hits.
On Your Feet loses steam when the melodramatic plot takes over in a second act that concentrates on family and romantic issues leading up to the bus crash that almost kills Gloria.

Let it immediately be said, audiences will certainly get their money's worth at On Your Feet! if they're enamored of the hot-hot music spread around the globe in tandem by Gloria (Ana Villafane, standing in for the real thing and with energy to spare) and hubby Emilio (Josh Segarra, soigné and sexy as hell in this incarnation).
The musical biography of Gloria and Emilio Estefan is a crowd-pleasing celebration of Latin music and culture, even if it hits familiar biographical beats.
Mitchell's direction is a great help, as is the enormously likable and often ferociously talented cast he has assembled.
The line is cheesy and crowd-rousing.
The fans who are the core audience to fill the giant Marquis Theater will thrill to the vibrantly staged songs they know and love and the Latino empowerment elements of Alexander Dinelaris's book.

On Your Feet is as much by-the-numbers as any other Broadway bio or juke box musical, but when the numbers are '1-2-3'...the average theatergoer will surely find it easier to forgive the formulaic aspects of the show.
Despite its pushy title, "On Your Feet!" — where audience members are dragooned from their seats to prance up the aisle with cast members for the first-act finale — is hard to dislike.
But much of this would be at least as effective (and probably more so) if the focus were more firmly on the music than on the Estefans.
It’s so self-congratulatory that one gets the impression that they personally vetted every line.
Still, On Your Feet is recommended only to the most diehard of fans.
As self-promoting hagiographies go, “On Your Feet!” makes “Trump: The Art of the Deal” look downright modest.

Given Villafane’s star-making portrayal and the strength of the Estefan song catalogue – which includes such hits as “1-2-3” and “Live for Loving You” -- you can’t help but wish she was in a somewhat sturdier vehicle than this one, which too often plays out like a so-so Latin version of “Beautiful.”
"On Your Feet!" which opened Thursday, is a fine addition to the ranks of jukebox musicals.

"Alexander Dinelaris’ deftly written script and Jerry Mitchell’s wonderfully inventive direction pretty much overcome the by-the-numbers feel and laboured approach than can afflict biographical jukebox musicals.
This is part musical, part concert, part love story and 100% pure inspiration.
Neither show is advancing the art form but they're both great fun.
'On Your Feet' will most likely get you on your feet and that's a good thing.
Ana Villafañe is outstanding and the show is totally worth it just to see her.
Even though the show leaves much to be desired, the one element that stands above everything else is Villafañe’s star-is-born performance.
For while this new show, playing at the Marquis Theatre, features a by-the-numbers rise-to-fame book by Alexander Dinelaris that can dull the senses, it also has some electrifying elements...
Unfortunately, it's just not all that interesting.
Director Jerry Mitchell seamlessly brings together all the elements that make On Your Feet! such a crowd-winning pleasure.
'On Your Feet' is the type of feel-good production that so many jukebox musicals strive to achieve but rarely actually do.
That comeback is the stirring climax of the musical, which otherwise is your basic rags-to-riches tale done with just enough tartness to avoid too much sentimentality.
Besides, Tony Award winner Jerry Mitchell directs everything nicely with his usual entertaining touches, making On Your Feet! a “Gloria-fied” hit.
Go for the music and the dancing and try to ignore the book.

cn.t: Critics find this Gloria Estefan bio-musical formulaic but infectious, with energetic performances and irresistible hit songs compensating for a predictable, paint-by-numbers story that rarely breaks new ground.

sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Marquis Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.
Farther from the stage than center orchestra — less up-close, but the sound still carries well.
At 1,611 seats, Marquis Theatre is one of the larger Broadway houses — far side mezzanine seats sit well off-axis and a long way from the stage.

vs.sum: The Marquis Theatre offers excellent comfort with spacious seating and good sightlines from most areas, although the ambiance is somewhat lacking due to its modern, hotel-integrated design. Facilities are well-equipped with ample restrooms and concessions, making it a convenient choice for theatergoers.

acc.note: Elevator via Marriott Marquis hotel. 10 wheelchair spaces. No elevator to Mezzanine.
